[LLM] Stage-4 implant written to /tmp/p<random>.js and executed by freshly dropped Bun binary Exploitation High
Detects the Miasma Stage-4 execution handoff: a randomly-named JS file at `/tmp/p<random>.js` (the decrypted 634 KB obfuscator.io payload) being executed by the Bun binary that the downloader just dropped under /tmp. This parent→child shape is article-specific and impossible to legitimately reproduce in normal CI. Rationale: Article explicitly states `_p` is written to `/tmp/p<random>.js` and executed via the freshly downloaded Bun binary — both paths are pinned to /tmp, parent is node, child is bun, and the JS filename matches `p[a-z0-9]+.js`. Regex on the cmdline anchors the random-naming convention without over-fitting on a specific suffix.
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1140 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let LookbackDays = 14d;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where FileName =~ "bun" or FileName =~ "bun.exe"
| where FolderPath startswith "/tmp/" or FolderPath has @"\Temp\"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/tmp/p[A-Za-z0-9]{3,}\.js"
   or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\\Temp\\p[A-Za-z0-9]{3,}\.js"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 14d;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("bun","bun.exe")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","node.exe")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/tmp/p[A-Za-z0-9]{3,}\.js"
   or TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @"\\Temp\\p[A-Za-z0-9]{3,}\.js"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] CI runner reading cloud-provider credential env files immediately after npm install Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the Miasma credential-harvest stage: the Stage-4 implant enumerates GitHub Actions secrets, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm, and CircleCI credential locations. Detects node/bun processes reading the well-known credential paths within minutes of an npm install on the same host, which is highly anomalous on CI runners. Rationale: Article enumerates the exact secret stores the implant harvests (GitHub Actions, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm tokens, CircleCI). I include the canonical credential file paths for each + GitHub Actions runner internals (`_runner_file_commands`, `RUNNER_TOKEN`). DistinctTargets >= 2 cuts noise from a single legitimate AWS CLI in a JS test. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/ • https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.005 T1528

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Dashlane password manager users locked out by brute force attacks

BleepingComputer
2026-06-01 4 use cases 2 techniques 3 kill-chain phases detected

Multiple Dashlane users have been locked out of their accounts following brute-force attacks that attempted logins from distant locations and unknown devices. [...]

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Dashlane brute-force lockout / new-device verification emails to corporate mailboxes (May-Jun 2026 campaign)
[LLM] Dashlane brute-force lockout / new-device verification emails to corporate mailboxes (May-Jun 2026 campaign) Actions on Objectives Medium
Identifies corporate users who received legitimate Dashlane suspension or new-device verification emails during the May 31 - Jun 1 2026 brute-force campaign. These mails (e.g. 'Your account has been temporarily suspended for security reasons...didn't enter the correct token after several tries') mean the attacker reached the account-targeting stage at Dashlane's auth tier for that user; the SOC should proactively rotate the user's master password, revoke active sessions, and watch the user for follow-on phishing. Rationale: Anchors on article-specific signals: Dashlane sender domain (dashlane.com / mail.dashlane.com), May 31 2026 campaign start window per Dashlane status page, and Dashlane's exact suspension-mail phrasing reported by The Register / Help Net Security ('Your account has been temporarily suspended ... didn't enter the correct token after several tries'). Aggregating per-recipient with EmailCount >= 2 raises confidence that the user was actively targeted (one-off legit new-device setup will normally produce one mail, not several). Cross-checked Dashlane status page (status.dashlane.com), The Register and Help Net Security write-ups confirming KR/RU source IPs and email phrasing; skipped image fetch since the in-article notice.jpeg is a UI screenshot of the same Dashlane email already quoted in the body. Cross-checked against: • https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/06/01/password-manager-dashlane-suspends-customer-accounts-amid-brute-force-attacks/5248991 • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/06/01/dashlane-brute-force-attack-user-accounts/ • https://cyberinsider.com/dashlane-hit-by-brute-force-campaign-triggering-account-suspensions/ • https://status.dashlane.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1110/003/
ATT&CKT1110 T1110.003 T1078.004
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email
let CampaignStart = datetime(2026-05-31T00:00:00Z);
let DashlaneDomains = dynamic(["dashlane.com","mail.dashlane.com","notify.dashlane.com"]);
let DashlaneSubjectTokens = dynamic(["suspended","verification code","new device","verify your","sign-in attempt","temporarily suspended","didn't enter the correct token"]);
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > CampaignStart - 1d and Timestamp < CampaignStart + 14d
| where SenderFromDomain in~ (DashlaneDomains)
   or SenderMailFromDomain in~ (DashlaneDomains)
| where Subject has_any (DashlaneSubjectTokens)
   or Subject has_any ("Dashlane", "new sign-in")
| where DeliveryAction in~ ("Delivered", "DeliveredAsSpam")
| summarize EmailCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen  = max(Timestamp),
            Subjects  = make_set(Subject, 10),
            Senders   = make_set(SenderFromAddress, 5),
            MsgIds    = make_set(NetworkMessageId, 10)
        by RecipientEmailAddress
| extend WindowHours = datetime_diff('hour', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| extend RiskNote = case(
        EmailCount >= 3, "3+ Dashlane brute-force notifications - very likely targeted",
        EmailCount == 2, "2 Dashlane notifications - investigate user",
        "single Dashlane notification - confirm with user")
| order by EmailCount desc, LastSeen desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — WordPress malware campaign hides payloads in Steam profiles
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] WordPress backdoor authentication via tEcaKKXEsb cookie or new_code POST parameter · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] WordPress server-side outbound to Steam Community (C2-via-profile-comments) · [LLM] WordPress server / browser egress to hello-mywordl[.]info (stage-2 JS loader) · [LLM] PHP / web-runtime process spawning cURL with SSL verification disabled · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] WordPress server-side outbound to Steam Community (C2-via-profile-comments) Command & Control Medium
Hunts for WordPress/web-server hosts making outbound calls to steamcommunity.com — the GoDaddy-tracked campaign uses Steam profile comments as a dead-drop C2 (invisible Unicode encodes a stage-2 URL). Web servers should never legitimately need to read Steam profiles. Rationale: Anchored on the article's central TTP — server-side fetch of Steam profile comments as the C2 channel. Web servers (php-fpm/apache/nginx/w3wp) reaching steamcommunity.com is the smell; legitimate user-driven Steam browsing happens from workstations, never from the server-side LAMP/LEMP runtime. Domain confirmed in BleepingComputer body and GoDaddy report referenced in article. Cross-checked against: • https://www.godaddy.com/resources/news/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1102/001/
ATT&CKT1102.001 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

| order by Timestamp desc

(ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (SteamHosts)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Query=DnsQuery, QueryType=DnsQueryTypeName, Src="ImDnsActivity"),
(ImNetworkSession

  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SrcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Query=coalesce(Url,DstHostname), QueryType="NetSession", Src="ImNetworkSession"),

  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csReferer has "steamcommunity.com" or csUriQuery has "steamcommunity.com"

[LLM] WordPress backdoor authentication via tEcaKKXEsb cookie or new_code POST parameter Installation High
Detects inbound HTTP POST requests containing the campaign-specific authentication cookie 'tEcaKKXEsb' or the 'new_code' parameter the backdoor uses to ingest base64-encoded PHP. Both strings are unique to this GoDaddy-reported family and survive obfuscation rotation. Rationale: Two needle-in-haystack strings called out verbatim by GoDaddy and quoted in the article — 'tEcaKKXEsb' cookie and 'new_code' POST parameter — that have no benign reason to appear in inbound traffic. Any single hit is investigable. Defender/Falcon left empty because EDR doesn't reliably capture L7 request bodies/cookies; these only surface in web-tier / WAF telemetry. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/wordpress-malware-campaign-hides-payloads-in-steam-profiles/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
union isfuzzy=true
(AppServiceHTTPLogs
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where CsMethod =~ "POST"
  | where Cookie has "tEcaKKXEsb" or CsUriQuery has "new_code="
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=CsHost, ClientIP=CIp, Method=CsMethod, Uri=CsUriStem, Query=CsUriQuery, Cookie, UA=UserAgent, Status=ScStatus, Src="AppServiceHTTPLogs"),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
  | where RequestCookies has "tEcaKKXEsb" or RequestURL has "new_code="
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=DestinationHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Method=RequestMethod, Uri=RequestURL, Query=RequestURL, Cookie=RequestCookies, UA=RequestClientApplication, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), Src="CommonSecurityLog"),
(W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csMethod =~ "POST"
  | where csUriQuery has "new_code=" or csUriStem has "new_code="
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, ClientIP=cIP, Method=csMethod, Uri=csUriStem, Query=csUriQuery, Cookie="<not-logged>", UA=csUserAgent, Status=tostring(scStatus), Src="W3CIISLog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)

[LLM] WordPress server / browser egress to hello-mywordl[.]info (stage-2 JS loader) Command & Control High
Alerts on any DNS/HTTP egress to hello-mywordl[.]info — the article's named stage-2 domain serving the injected JavaScript disguised as asahi-jquery-min-bundle / lodash.core.min.js. Catches both the WP server fetching the payload and end-user browsers loading the injected library on infected sites. Rationale: Single named domain IOC (hello-mywordl[.]info) called out verbatim by BleepingComputer / GoDaddy as the stage-2 loader URL. A multi-source union (DNS + L7 web + WAF) catches both the WP origin pulling the payload and end-user clients loading the injected JS. No legitimate use of this domain. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/wordpress-malware-campaign-hides-payloads-in-steam-profiles/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105 T1059.007
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let BadDomain = dynamic(["hello-mywordl.info"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where RemoteUrl has_any (BadDomain)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Src="NetworkEvent"),
(DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType in ("DnsQueryResponse","InboundConnectionAccepted") and RemoteUrl has_any (BadDomain)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Src="DeviceEvent")
| order by Timestamp desc
let BadDomain = dynamic(["hello-mywordl.info"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Name has_any (BadDomain)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Indicator=Name, Type="DNS", Src="DnsEvents"),
(ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (BadDomain)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Indicator=DnsQuery, Type="DNS", Src="ImDnsActivity"),
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Url has_any (BadDomain) or HttpHostName has_any (BadDomain)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Indicator=coalesce(Url,HttpHostName), Type="Web", Src="ImWebSession"),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationHostName has_any (BadDomain) or RequestURL has_any (BadDomain)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DeviceName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Indicator=coalesce(RequestURL,DestinationHostName), Type="CEF", Src="CommonSecurityLog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] PHP / web-runtime process spawning cURL with SSL verification disabled Command & Control Medium
Hunts for web-server processes (php-fpm, php-cgi, apache2, nginx, w3wp) invoking curl with -k / --insecure / CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER=false. The article explicitly names disabled SSL verification in cURL as a campaign tell — used to talk to Steam and to hello-mywordl[.]info without TLS pinning hassle. Rationale: The article explicitly lists 'disabled SSL verification in cURL requests' as an IOC. Pairing that flag with a web-runtime parent (php-fpm/apache/nginx/w3wp) is high-signal — sysadmins debugging with curl -k do so from interactive shells, not from PHP-FPM workers. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/wordpress-malware-campaign-hides-payloads-in-steam-profiles/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1573 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let WebSvcParents = dynamic(["php-fpm","php","php-cgi","php.exe","php-cgi.exe","httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (WebSvcParents)
| where FileName in~ ("curl","curl.exe","wget")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\s-k\b|--insecure\b|--no-check-certificate\b|VERIFYPEER\s*=\s*(0|false))"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let WebSvcParents = dynamic(["php-fpm","php","php-cgi","php.exe","php-cgi.exe","httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any (WebSvcParents) or ActingProcessName has_any (WebSvcParents)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("curl","curl.exe","wget")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\s-k\b|--insecure\b|--no-check-certificate\b|VERIFYPEER\s*=\s*(0|false))"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: PHP / Web-Runtime Spawning cURL with SSL Verification Disabled
id: f3b8d2a4-1c6e-49a7-9b1f-2c8d4a6e7711
description: Web-server processes (php-fpm, apache2, nginx, w3wp) spawning curl with -k/--insecure — matches the GoDaddy-reported WordPress Steam-comment campaign which disables TLS verification when fetching its stage-2 loader.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/wordpress-malware-campaign-hides-payloads-in-steam-profiles/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/01
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1573
  - attack.t1505.003
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/php-fpm'
      - '/php-cgi'
      - '/php'
      - '\php.exe'
      - '\php-cgi.exe'
      - '/httpd'
      - '/apache2'
      - '/nginx'
      - '\w3wp.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '\curl.exe'
  selection_args:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -k '
      - ' --insecure'
      - 'VERIFYPEER=0'
      - 'VERIFYPEER=false'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_args
level: medium
(source:linux.auditd @process.parent.name:(php-fpm OR php OR php-cgi OR apache2 OR httpd OR nginx) @process.name:curl @process.command_line:(*" -k "* OR *"--insecure"* OR *VERIFYPEER=0* OR *VERIFYPEER=false*)) OR (source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\php-cgi.exe OR *\php.exe OR *\w3wp.exe) @Image:(*\curl.exe OR *\CURL.EXE) @CommandLine:(*" -k "* OR *"--insecure"*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/curl(\.exe)?$/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/(php-fpm|php-cgi|php|httpd|apache2|nginx|w3wp\.exe)$/i
| regex("(?i)(\\s-k\\b|--insecure|VERIFYPEER\\s*=\\s*(0|false))", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("php-fpm","php","php-cgi","php.exe","php-cgi.exe","httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe") AND Processes.process_name IN ("curl","curl.exe") AND (Processes.process="* -k *" OR Processes.process="*--insecure*" OR Processes.process="*VERIFYPEER*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("php-fpm","php","php-cgi","php.exe","php-cgi.exe","httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe") AND Processes.process_name IN ("curl","curl.exe") AND (Processes.process="* -k *" OR Processes.process="*--insecure*" OR Processes.process="*VERIFYPEER*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:

            - '\powershell.exe'

    selection_args:

            - 'Invoke-Expression'

            - '-w hidden'

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1") or SHA1 in~ ("f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1") or MD5 in~ ("f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1") or SHA1 in~ ("f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1") or MD5 in~ ("f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

// Article-specific bespoke detection — WordPress malware campaign hides payloads in Steam profiles
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named

DeviceProcessEvents

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,

| where (FileName in~ ("lodash.core.min.js"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
